items.title: Single-item response of item 1 includes its type Footwear next to its brand
covers: AC3: GET /api/catalog/items/{id} includes the item's type (id and name)
AC3: as it already includes its brand
items.reason: AC3 is the API contract the page depends on: without `.Include(CatalogType)` the item arrives with `catalogType: null` and the page renders an empty Category. The functional layer runs the real EF query against Postgres, which is where a missing include shows up, and is cheaper than going through the UI. Both API versions are checked because the route is mapped on the shared `api` group.

items.title: Single-item response of item 99 carries the same type id and name as the catalog types list
covers: AC2: Category is the name of the product's catalog type, the same name the type filter shows
AC3: type id and name
items.reason: AC2 requires the shown category to be the same name the type filter shows; the filter is fed by `GET /api/catalog/catalogtypes`. Checking a second item with a different type (7, Navigation) also proves the include follows the item's own `catalogTypeId` instead of returning a fixed or first type. Functional is the cheapest layer that compares the two real endpoints.

items.title: Rest of the product page is unchanged for a signed-in shopper

items.title: Single-item request for an id just past the catalog still returns 404 after the type include
covers: AC3: GET /api/catalog/items/{id} (query changed to include the type)
AC3: the endpoint's other behaviour is unchanged
items.reason: AC3 changes the query of `GetItemById` by adding `.Include(ci => ci.CatalogType)`. An include that turned the lookup into an inner join on a missing row, or a handler that started dereferencing the type before the null check, would turn a missing item into a 500 or a 200 with an empty body. The id is 102, just past the last seeded item (101), so it is the boundary between found and not found. Functional is the cheapest layer that runs the real EF query against Postgres.

items.title: Single-item request with id 0 is still rejected with 400 before any lookup
covers: AC3: GET /api/catalog/items/{id} (query changed to include the type)
AC3: the endpoint's other behaviour is unchanged
items.reason: The handler edited for AC3 validates the id before running the query. Id 0 is just outside the valid range (item 1 is the lowest valid id, covered by TC-TYPE-1-01), so this case pins the lower boundary of the same handler and proves the change did not move or drop the validation. Functional is the cheapest layer that exercises the real route and its ProblemDetails response.
